content: Simplified Rugby: Fun Facts & Common Questions For those new to Rugby, we’ve included some fun facts and common questions. For those not new to Rugby, please be gracious about the explanations provided. Our goal is to give simple, easy-to-understand overviews. Fun Facts Scoreboard Fun Facts & Common Questions The sport of Rugby is older than American Football and younger than International Football (what we call “Soccer” in America). Bonus Fun Fact: American Football adopted pieces of Rugby and Soccer into their rules when they originated. What is “15s”? 15s refers to teams playing 15 players vs 15 players. For High School, this version is played in the Spring. Each game roster is maxed at 23 players: 15 starters and 8 finishers. High School games are 60 minutes with two 30 minute halves. (For comparison, all levels above high school play 80 minute games with two 40 minute halves.) What is “7s”? 7s refers to teams playing 7 players vs 7 players. For High School, this version is played in the Fall. Games are 14 minutes with two 7 minute halves. Passing – Backwards and parallel only. Forward passing is penalized. Scoring – Try – 5 points. A player physically touches the ball on the ground in the end zone. If the ball doesn’t touch the ground there is no score. Conversion – 2 points. Between the goal posts and above the middle bar. Think of this as the “kicking points after a Try”. The kicking location is pulled straight back from where the Try occurred, not centered in the middle of the field like American Football. In 15s, the conversion is done from a tee. In 7s, the conversion is drop-kicked. Drop-Kick – 3 points. Between the goal posts and above the middle bar. Occurs during active play and can be from any part of the field. Penalty Goal – 3 points. Between the goal posts and above the middle bar. This is an option available when a penalty is awarded. The non-penalized team can choose Scrum or to kick, aka “Penalty Goal”. Penalty Try – 7 points. Awarded when a player would have scored a try but was prevented from doing so by foul play from the opposing team. Equipment – Mouth guard. (Get a good one.) Cleats – they must be all plastic or all metal. Cannot be “bi-material.” This is important. Know what you are buying, Keep Rugby safe. Tackling – Full contact; there is an art to it. content: Westside Rugby Football Club The Westside Rugby Football Club, USA Rugby, and Rugby Indiana are committed to ensuring a positive youth rugby experience. We provide league-wide benefits for our coaches, parents, and players of all ages (flag through high school varsity and adult leagues). Registration has Opened for Spring 2026! Registration is not required to check us out!! Come to practice and we’ll help you on next steps. Rugby is a great sport to improve confidence, physical and mental health, whether played competitively or recreationally. Kids that play rugby enjoy several physical, social, and mental benefits, which will bode well with them as they approach their adulthood and beyond. It also promotes teamwork, keeps kids out of mischief, and boosts the concentration level of a child. Most importantly Westside Rugby provides a sense of belonging and family and once you are family, you are family for life. Furthermore, rugby offers kids - whether small or large, slim or heavy, short or stout, agile or speedster - equal opportunities to run with the ball, pass it, and play defense. There is a position for every body type out there. In rugby, everyone participates that way; nobody gets left out. * as of 1/22/2026 Our Home Pitch is Sycamore Elementary School, 7878 E County Rd 100 N, Avon, IN 46123 - Open Map Serving Our Rugby Community Since 2009 The Westside Rugby Football Club began in 2009, inspired by a group of rugby players from the Westside of Indianapolis who wanted to give their kids the best coaching experience. Year after year our Rugby and Touch sections have grown enormously. We share expertise and benefit from talented coaches many who still play rugby for the adult section of the WRFC (the Outcasts) and some who regularly play or coach for the Marion and IUPUI college teams, making us stand out as a junior rugby club in Indiana. One of the goals of the founders of the WRFC was to provide a unique transition from youth to junior to adult rugby. content: Registration Help Westside Rugby Football Club is part of Rugby Indiana. Rugby Indiana uses the Rugby Xplorer Registration Tool. Please see the information below for registration instructions. Register Now Registration is not required to check us out!! Come to practice and we’ll help you on next steps. Registration has Opened for Spring 2026! From https://westsiderugbyfootballclub.org/ Click on the “Register Now” Button Click on the “Login” tile. Sign in with the username and password that you set up when registering you and/or your child for the Rugby club. (This sign-in is the “Rugby Xplorer” account.) Once signed into your Rugby Xplorer account, click “Register” from the left-hand side menu. From the “Play Rugby” menu, click on the “Find a Club” tile. Choose the player you want to register from the listed people and click “Next”. Search for “Westside Rugby”. When it appears, choose it and click “Next”. Choose the appropriate Role, Registration Type, and Duration of “Season”. Click “Next”. Continue filling out the form and submit.
